newsitem.title: USA: IPO issuance climbs, quality a question - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: IPO issuance climbs, quality a question - Barron's.

text.p: Wall Street brought nearly 700 new stock issues to the marketplace in 1996 through December 10, but the initial public offering surge has contributed to unease about overall stock market direction, Barron's said.

"The peak in new stock issuance in 1983 was followed by a significant market correction that lasted through 1984," Robert Natale, vice president of equity research at Standard & Poor's, said in the December 16 issue of the investor paper.

Analysts said some deals were done prematurely. Garrett Van Wagoner of Van Wagoner Capital Management said Cardiac Pathways Corp and CardioGenesis Corp, which develop caridac-treatment technologies, would have fared better if they delayed their initial public offerings.
According to Montgomery Securities, this year's IPOs rose an average 14 percent apiece, versus last year's average 37 percent gains, the weekly newspaper said.
One analyst was quoted in Barron's as saying the high volume in this year's deals necessitated an enormous -- "daunting" -- amount of research for potential investors.
Biotech stocks were among the year's worst victims, the newspaper said, citing Avigen Inc and Microcide Pharmaceuticals Inc.
